stem: A page looks correct, but its DOM order does not match the visual layout. Which test best reveals whether keyboard focus follows the visual order?

options.text: Tab through the page and watch the focus order.
options.rationale: Keyboard focus follows the DOM, so tabbing shows whether the sequence matches what sighted users see.

options.text: Run an automated HTML validator and check for markup errors.
options.rationale: Valid markup can still be in an order that does not match the visual layout.

options.text: Check the page's text and background colors with a contrast analyzer.
options.rationale: Contrast affects readability, not the sequence in which focus moves.

options.text: Open the page at 200% zoom and check for horizontal scrolling.
options.rationale: Zoom tests enlargement, not the order of focusable elements.

explanation: Keyboard focus follows the document order. If CSS places content in a different visual order, keyboard and screen reader users can meet controls in an unexpected sequence. Tabbing through the page and comparing the focus path with the layout exposes the mismatch; validation, contrast, and zoom checks do not.

references.title: W3C WAI — Understanding Success Criterion 2.4.3: Focus Order

author: Oxypteros
